raw:
These hypotheses come from general knowledge of NAS-Bench-201, not from running anything. In this space the direct paths 0->3 (edge 3) and the conv-heavy routes matter most, and the output node needs at least one informative incoming edge.

1. Setting edge 4 (1->3) to nor_conv_3x3 helps less when edge 5 (2->3) is already nor_conv_3x3. Both feed the output, so the second strong conv has diminishing returns.
2. Setting edge 0 (0->1) to nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 4 (1->3) is nor_conv_3x3. A strong first hop only pays off if its output reaches node 3 through a capable edge.
3. Setting edge 3 (0->3) to skip_connect helps less when edge 5 (2->3) is nor_conv_3x3. The conv route already supplies capacity and the gradient path is largely redundant.
4. Setting edge 3 (0->3) to none hurts more when edge 4 (1->3) is none. Removing a route when alternatives are gone cuts off the output.
5. Setting edge 5 (2->3) to none hurts more when edge 3 (0->3) is none. Fewer alternative routes to the output means damage is concentrated.
6. Setting edge 1 (0->2) to nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 5 (2->3) is nor_conv_1x1 than when it is none. This is a conditional effect: node 2's features only matter if they propagate.

In 6, "than when it does not" includes every other op, so the claim is mixed. I'm keeping it with the condition at edge 5 being none, restated below as "lower".

7. Setting edge 2 (1->2) to nor_conv_3x3 helps less when edge 1 (0->2) is nor_conv_3x3. Node 2 already has a strong conv input, so the extra route adds little.
8. Setting edge 0 (0->1) to none hurts more when edge 3 (0->3) is none. With the direct path gone, the route through node 1 is the main one.
9. Setting edge 4 (1->3) to avg_pool_3x3 is less harmful when edge 3 (0->3) is nor_conv_3x3. A strong direct conv path makes up for the weaker pooled route.
10. Setting edge 5 (2->3) to nor_conv_3x3 helps less when edge 3 (0->3) is nor_conv_3x3. A strong direct conv already supplies most of the representational gain, so there are diminishing returns.
